title: Stream boundary epoching and lightweight replay verification for multi-stream CUDA graphs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Symptoms observed: sporadic token-level divergence and rare invalid KV lookups when reusing CUDA graphs across concurrent decode streams. Root cause hypothesis: race between graph replay and per-stream prefill completion, compounded by cross-stream kernel reuse and optimized kernel selection that assumes a stable KV epoch. This ticket proposes a layered approach: (1) introduce a lightweight per-request 'epoch stamp' for KV cache state at prefill completion, (2) enforce a stream-fence/epoch check before a graph replay is committed to a stream, and (3) add an opt-in 'verify mode' that performs a low-cost hash comparison of a subset of KV tensors after replay to detect silent drift. The goal is to eliminate correctness anomalies while minimizing steady-state latency impact.
acceptance_criteria: Canary traffic shows zero token-delta regressions over 72h compared to baseline for mixed stream workloads
Verify-mode flags mismatches reproducibly and produces a deterministic diagnostic trace that reproduces locally
End-to-end median latency increase under typical load < 1.5% with epoching enabled and sampled verification disabled
Fallback path (stream-sync) triggers automatically if epoch check fails and recovers the request without corruption
technical_notes: Design: stamp a small 64-bit epoch ID into the request context when prefill finishes. Persist lightweight epoch metadata in the per-stream metadata header used by the graph replay path. Before launching a cached CUDA graph, replay path checks epoch equality; if mismatch, either (a) pause and synchronize with prefill completion, (b) re-capture a stream-local graph, or (c) fall back to single-stream decode. Verification: sample the top-level KV tensors (first/last N bytes) and compute an XXH64; comparisons are cheap and run on-device. Synchronization primitives: use cudaEvent + streamWaitEvent and avoid global device-wide synchronization. Kernel selection interactions: ensure kernel-selection table keys include epoch fingerprint so we don't reuse kernels tuned for mismatched occupancy/quant profiles. Trade-offs: adds a few micro-kernel ops and potential stalls on edge cases; incremental rollout and sampling mitigates cost. Implementation boundaries: keep epoch metadata as a 64-bit token to avoid bloating trace payloads.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: implement epoch stamping and in-memory epoch checks behind a feature flag (dev-only). Phase 2: add sampled on-device verify-mode (canary) and automated alerting for mismatch rate. Phase 3: enable epoch checks by default, verification sampling at 0.1%, and monitor latency/cost. Phase 4: if stable, raise sampling to 1% and enable for Dedicated clusters. Rollback: feature flag kills epoch check and verification; fallback path always available to avoid customer-visible failures.
tests: Deterministic fuzz harness that alternates prefill/replay ordering and asserts identical outputs
Long-run mixed-concurrency soak (72h) with synthetic traffic and token-delta histogram collection
Chaos test: simulate preemption and stream migration while running graph replays
Performance microbenchmarks for median/99p latency with epoch checks enabled vs disabled

2026-03-03 Engineering PRD feedback (Lena Kim): add explicit heuristics when to prefer re-capture vs fallback to single-stream for degraded hardware (preemptible GPUs).
